Answer: B
Reason: The radiograph demonstrates multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules, some of which appear cavitating (indicated by the upper arrow), along with a moderate left-sided pleural effusion and blunting of the right costophrenic angle (lower arrow). These findings, particularly the cavitating nodules and asymmetric effusion in the absence of marked cardiomegaly, are classic for septic pulmonary emboli.
